newsitem.title: UK: Zinc T/C deal seen as tilt towards smelters.
newsitem.headline: Zinc T/C deal seen as tilt towards smelters.

text.p: Wednesday's benchmark treatment charge deal between Metaleurop SA and Cominco Ltd is expected to set the tone for the rest of the zinc industry for 1997 terms and appears to favour the smelters, analysts here said.
Metaleurop and Cominco settled their benchmark treatment charge for concentrates at $186/tonne basis LME cash at $1,100.
"This is certainly higher than people were talking about. The smelters were looking for a rollover (from 1996), and they have virtually got that," said Graham Deller of CRU International.
" I am surprised that it is quite that high...and that will be quite a signal," another analyst said.
Canada's Cominco is one of the world's biggest zinc and lead miners, with France's Metaleurop of France a leading global smelter of zinc.
The deal was announced at the American Zinc Association (AZA) industry meeting in Arizona. It includes an escalator of 20 cents per lb, and a de-escalator of 15 cents a lb.
Others said that the deal had to be seen in context of the basis price of $1,100, versus the 1996 basis of $1,000.
"The basis price is high, which does make a diference...but it (the T/C) is slightly higher than what had been expected," another analyst said.
The new benchmark deal for 1997 will equate to a downside of $170 per tonne on a base LME cash price of $1,000.
Last year's benchmark price was settled at $190 per tonne, basis LME price of $1,000 per tonne. Escalators last year were 13 to 15 cents.
Metaleurop has also booked two other deals with mining companies at similar levels, which indicates that the zinc "mating season" may be drawing to a close, traders said.
Recent mine cutbacks coincided with the start of this process, and could have suggested that miners would have the upper hand.

The high profile cutback was Canada's Faro mine, which closed temporarily in December 1996. Cominco has a private placement of shares in Faro's owners Anvil Range, which equates to a 28 percent stake.
Meanwhile, zinc prices have risen strongly recently, with three months reaching two-year highs of $1,190 a tonne on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Wednesday.
This could well encourage mine-starts, amd may have strengthened the smelter position in the current talks, traders said.
